questions.text: The FSM (Finite State Machine) machine pictured in the figure above
questions.solution:
Reading bits from the LSB with the start state:
- input 1 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] output 0 and go to the "carry" state (1 + 1 = 10)
- in the carry state, 1 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 0 (carry continues), 0 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 1 and go to the "no carry" state
- in the no-carry state, bits are copied unchanged
- a first input 0 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] output 1 (no carry)

This adds 1 to the number.

Answer: Increments a given bit pattern by 1

questions.text: CFG  (Context Free Grammar) is not closed under:
questions.solution:
Context-free languages are closed under union, Kleene star and concatenation (product), but not under complementation (or intersection).

Answer: Complementation

questions.text:
Given a language L, define [latex]L^{i}[/latex] as follows:
[latex]L^{0}=\{\varepsilon \} [/latex]
[latex]L^{i}=L^{i-1} \cdot L [/latex] for all [latex] i \gt 0[/latex]
The order of a language L is defined as the smallest k such that [latex]L^{k}=L^{k+1}[/latex]. Consider the language L1 (over alphabet 0) accepted by the following automaton.

The order of L1 is ______
questions.solution:
From the automaton, [latex]L_1=\{\epsilon\}\cup0(00)^*[/latex] (empty or odd number of 0s).
- [latex]L_1^1=L_1[/latex] (no even lengths except 0)
- [latex]L_1^2[/latex]: odd + odd gives every even length, so [latex]L_1^2=0^*[/latex]
- [latex]L_1^3=0^*=L_1^2[/latex]

Smallest k with [latex]L^k=L^{k+1}[/latex] is 2.

Answer: 2

questions.text:
Consider the following problems. L(G) denotes the language generated by a grammar G. L(M) denotes the language accepted by a machine M.

(I) For an unrestricted grammar G and a string w, whether w[latex]\in [/latex]L(G)
(II) Given a Turing machine M, whether L(M) is regular
(III) Given two grammars G1 and G2, whether L(G1) = L(G2)
(IV) Given an NFA N, whether there is a deterministic PDA P such that N and P accept the same language.

Which one of the following statements is correct?
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- I: membership for unrestricted grammars = TM acceptance [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] undecidable.
- II: is L(M) regular (Rice) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] undecidable.
- III: equivalence of two grammars (even CFGs) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] undecidable.
- IV: an NFA's language is regular, and every regular language has a DPDA [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] the answer is always yes [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] decidable.

Answer: Only I, II and III are undecidable
